inspiration.observed_pattern: A MySQL compatibility corpus exercises UUID_TO_BIN and BIN_TO_UUID with the optional byte-order swap flag, malformed values, and NULL propagation.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as an independently authored binary-key audit. MariaDB 10.11.7 does not expose UUID_TO_BIN or BIN_TO_UUID, so the fixture expresses the deterministic UUID byte layouts with UNHEX, HEX, SUBSTRING, and CONCAT: canonical UUID groups are packed directly, and the swap form reorders the time fields before packing. A NULL key verifies propagation. The table, identifiers, UUID values, and audit purpose are new, and malformed inputs are omitted to keep the comparison focused on valid deterministic semantics.

fixture_notes: Keys 801 and 802 contain valid canonical UUIDs; key 803 is NULL. The report shows canonical and swapped binary encodings while preserving the NULL row.
determinism_notes: All key IDs, UUID literals, swap flags, projections, and ordering are fixed. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE binary_service_keys (key_id INT PRIMARY KEY, uuid_text CHAR(36) NULL)

steps.sql: SELECT key_id, LOWER(uuid_text) AS canonical_text, HEX(UNHEX(CONCAT(SUBSTRING(uuid_text, 1, 8), SUBSTRING(uuid_text, 10, 4), SUBSTRING(uuid_text, 15, 4), SUBSTRING(uuid_text, 20, 4), SUBSTRING(uuid_text, 25, 12)))) AS packed_hex, HEX(UNHEX(CONCAT(SUBSTRING(uuid_text, 15, 4), SUBSTRING(uuid_text, 10, 4), SUBSTRING(uuid_text, 1, 8), SUBSTRING(uuid_text, 20, 4), SUBSTRING(uuid_text, 25, 12)))) AS swapped_hex FROM binary_service_keys ORDER BY key_id

checks.sql: SELECT key_id, uuid_text FROM binary_service_keys ORDER BY key_id
